Voice typing now learns from your corrections. Fix a word it misheard — right where you pasted it, in whatever app you were dictating into — and Parley notices within a couple of seconds and offers to add the correction to your phrase dictionary (⌥↩ to accept, or just ignore it; decline the same pair twice and it stops asking). The watching is deliberately narrow: only the field Parley just pasted into, only for a minute, using the same Accessibility permission auto-paste already has. The diff is computed locally and thrown away — nothing about the field is stored or uploaded.

Dictionary phrases work on both ends of a transcription. They bias recognition itself — every provider gets them in its own dialect (Soniox context, Deepgram keyterms, AssemblyAI word boost, OpenAI and Gemini prompts) — and any misheard variant you've taught still gets rewritten to the right spelling before the text is shown or pasted. Meeting transcription and uploaded recordings read the same dictionary, so a name taught once is right everywhere.

A Dictionary panel in Settings lists everything you've taught (and takes manual additions), the voice-typing history gains an inline correct-and-learn editor for apps whose text Accessibility can't read, and the MCP server grows four tools — list, add, update, delete — so external AI tooling can manage the dictionary too. Voice typing also now sends proper language hints, which it never did before.
